original_query: select ps_partkey, sum(ps_supplycost * ps_availqty) as value from partsupp, supplier, nation where ps_suppkey = s_suppkey and s_nationkey = n_nationkey and n_name = 'IRAN' group by ps_partkey having sum(ps_supplycost * ps_availqty) > ( select sum(ps_supplycost * ps_availqty) * 0.0001000000 from partsupp, supplier, nation where ps_suppkey = s_suppkey and s_nationkey = n_nationkey and n_name = 'IRAN' ) order by value desc;
rewritten_query:
SELECT ps_partkey, value
FROM (
    SELECT
        ps_partkey,
        value,
        SUM(value) OVER () * 0.0001000000 AS threshold
    FROM (
        SELECT
            ps_partkey,
            SUM(ps_supplycost * ps_availqty) AS value
        FROM partsupp
        JOIN supplier ON partsupp.ps_suppkey = supplier.s_suppkey
        JOIN nation ON supplier.s_nationkey = nation.n_nationkey
        WHERE nation.n_name = 'IRAN'
        GROUP BY ps_partkey
    ) AS part_totals
) AS part_values
WHERE value > threshold
ORDER BY value DESC;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Eliminate the duplicated uncorrelated scalar subquery that re-aggregates partsupp/supplier/nation for the threshold. Since the threshold equals the sum of all per-part group values times 0.0001, replace it with a window function SUM(value) OVER () computed over the grouped results, reducing partsupp from two full scans/aggregations to one.

Convert old comma-style joins to explicit JOIN ... ON syntax and push the nation filter ('IRAN') as a WHERE predicate; this keeps the same join semantics while improving readability and allowing the planner to hash-join the filtered supplier set cleanly.

Restructure the HAVING-based filtering into an outer WHERE over the aggregated/windowed subquery, since window function results cannot appear in HAVING/WHERE of the same SELECT level. This preserves semantics: filter groups whose value exceeds total*0.0001, ordered by value DESC.
